chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿAmrakī ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man whose garment is touched by a pig, and he did not wash it, then he remembers while he is in his salat (prayer): what should he do with it? He said: “If he has entered into his salat (prayer), then let him continue; and if he has not entered into his salat (prayer), then let him sprinkle water on whatever of his garment was affected, unless there is a trace in it, in which case he should wash it.”
And I asked him about a pig that drank from a vessel: what should be done with it? He said: “It should be washed seven times.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: Likewise, the ruling concerning the mouse and the gecko is that the place of the garment which they touched is sprinkled if they left no effect on it; and if they moistened it and left an effect on it, it is washed with water. This indicates it.

key_terms.أَثَرٌ: trace; a remaining sign of impurity that requires washing
key_terms.إِنَاءٍ: vessel; the container from which the pig drank
key_terms.ثَوْبِهِ: his garment; the clothing affected by impurity
key_terms.خِنْزِيرٌ: pig; an animal whose contact causes ritual impurity in this ruling
key_terms.سَبْعَ مَرَّاتٍ: seven times; the required number of washings for the vessel
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer); the prayer state in which the impurity is remembered
key_terms.فَلْيَنْضِحْ: let him sprinkle; applying water without full washing in the stated case
key_terms.يُغْسَلُ: it is washed; the prescribed purification method

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a pig touches clothing or drinks from a vessel in Shia hadith law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings regarding ritual impurity caused by a pig touching a garment or drinking from a vessel. It distinguishes between merely sprinkling water and fully washing based on whether a trace remains, and it also states that a vessel from which a pig drank must be washed seven times. The closing note extends a similar ruling to a mouse and a gecko when no visible effect is left.
